And indeed, it was only a few days ago that the Supreme Court interpreted a provision in our federal anti-discrimination law to prohibit discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation in the employment context. Of course, we need a statute that clarifies that. And, of course, you know, when I think about being black, I think about the fact that I was the only person in a crowded Democratic primary talking about the need for policing reform before the murder of George Floyd, right, before it became popular to talk about. And that is because I know what it's like to fear for my life and my safety and to be targeted and to be by law enforcement and to be adversely impacted by the systemic oppression that pervades our so-called criminal justice system. I call it a criminal legal system. And I bring those experiences to me into the policymaking process. I know how our laws adversely impact marginalized communities like the ones from which I come.
